answer: Commit-reveal beacon lottery. Before each epoch, an identity submits a secret seed commitment. At epoch close the public beacon fixes slot order as hash(seed, beacon), so repeated seeds collide and reveal duplication. Each attempt also needs a distinct network inlet and pays a nonrefundable fee plus an epoch-long compute lease; there is no shared haven that amortizes these costs across clones. Gaining k slots costs k separate leases and fees, and reusing one seed or inlet exposes the cluster.
